subject: POC capacity & success criteria - Acme AI (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kunal Iyer <kunal.iyer@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC capacity & success criteria - Acme AI (next steps)

Hi Priya / Kunal —

Great to meet you both this morning. Thanks for the deep dive on Acme's evaluation goals — this thread is a quick recap of the agreed POC approach and the immediate next steps so we can get capacity reserved and the SOW moving. Please flag anything I missed.

POC scope (recap)
- Goal: Validate latency & throughput for LLM-powered summarization and a short-context assistant across 10k daily active users (target subset).
- Models: r-instruct-large (baseline) + r-instruct-quant (cost-optimized).
- Workloads: mix of small chat (avg 60 tokens output) and longer summarization (avg 300 tokens). Peak concurrency estimated at ~120 concurrent requests during business hours.

Success criteria (Agreed)
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation <= 600ms for chat (60 tok) and <= 2.5s for summarization (300 tok).
2) Quality: ROUGE/LQual pass rate >= 85% on your eval set (we'll ingest sample prompts you shared).
3) Cost target: < $0.015 per 1k tokens served for baseline config (target for quantized path: 30% lower).
4) Reliability: no more than 1 incident causing > 5min outage during the 4-week POC.

Capacity proposal (what we need to reserve now)
- Reserved baseline: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) to guarantee sustained throughput.
- Autoscaling: allow scale-up to 8 GPUs for brief bursts (up to 30 minutes continuous) driven by queue depth. Burst capacity will be billed at on-demand rates.
- Warm-up/cache: we expect warm-up iterations (KV cache population) to require ~10k tokens per model variant; recommend a scripted warm-up run on day-0.

Operational ownership
- Redwood: reserve capacity, configure autoscale policy, provide runbook and telemetry dashboards (per-route latency/cost).
- Acme: provide eval dataset, quality rubric, and a technical contact for endpoint integration (Priya / Kunal).

Next steps (timeline)
1) Mar 23 — SOW & POC MAP review (attached).
2) Mar 24 — Capacity reservation confirmed by Redwood (we need headcount approval from sales ops).
3) Mar 25 — Day-0 warm-up + baseline run with your eval prompts.
4) Mar 26 - Apr 20 — 4-week active evaluation.

Attachments: ACME-POC-MAP-2026-03.pdf (POC plan), SOW-draft-Acme-POC.docx (SOW draft).

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm the eval dataset file and the owner we should expect to ingest?
- Any procurement or legal constraints that would slow capacity reservation?

Thanks — I'll loop in the rest of the team for capacity/pricing details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Priya — quick technical confirm:
- SKU: A100-40GB equivalent (NVIDIA A100 40GB) across Redwood Dedicated. We'll call out exact vCPU/bandwidth in the SOW.
- Autoscale cold-start: typically ~45–120s to spin up GPU workers and warm model weights; additional KV-cache warm-up is workload-dependent — plan ~10–15 minutes to reach steady-state latency for summarization once traffic hits peak. For short bursts (<=30m) you should expect the first 1–2 minutes of slightly elevated p95 while instances initialize.
- Warm-up recommendation: run scripted warm-up (we can provide) that hits top 20 prompts at production concurrency to populate caches. This reduces burst p95 by ~30–40%.
- Throughput estimate: for r-instruct-large (fp16): 4xA100 baseline should meet the estimated concurrency for chat; for summarization at 300 tok we recommend running quantized variant on baseline and moving heavier runs to burst if you want lower cost.

I'll attach a short runbook and warm-up script after internal review. Happy to schedule a tech sync if you want to go deeper.

Regards,
